stem: What limited the RT-PCR and microarray profiling of patch-pipette aspirates that preceded Patch-seq?
choices: Contamination from the extracellular solution
Small numbers of genes and/or cells
Loss of the electrophysiological recording
Inability to recover cell morphology
answer: Small numbers of genes and/or cells
label: Review · precursors

stem: What characterised the first attempt at single-cell RNA sequencing of neurons collected with a patch pipette (Qiu et al., 2012)?
choices: Thousands of cells but no morphology
High-quality data from cultured neurons only
Very few samples and low-quality sequencing data
Full transcriptomes but no electrophysiology
answer: Very few samples and low-quality sequencing data
label: Review · first attempt

stem: Why do Patch-seq protocols insist on strict RNase-free conditions during sample collection?
choices: RNases inhibit the template-switching oligonucleotide
RNase activity distorts the patch-clamp seal resistance
RNases degrade the biocytin used for morphology
RNases are ubiquitous and each cell holds very little mRNA
answer: RNases are ubiquitous and each cell holds very little mRNA
label: Review · RNase-free

stem: How is the recording pipette tip typically adjusted for Patch-seq, and why?
choices: Slightly larger, to ease aspiration of the cell contents
Slightly smaller, to improve the electrical seal
Slightly larger, to speed dye filling for morphology
Slightly smaller, to reduce glial contamination
answer: Slightly larger, to ease aspiration of the cell contents
label: Review · pipette tip

stem: Why do Patch-seq protocols use smaller than normal volumes of internal solution?
choices: To shorten the time needed to fill the neuron with dye
To avoid diluting the RNA and limit glass contact
To reduce the amount of calcium chelator reaching the cell
To keep the electrical seal stable during aspiration
answer: To avoid diluting the RNA and limit glass contact
label: Review · internal solution volume

stem: Which additives can be put in the Patch-seq internal solution to promote RNA preservation?
choices: Biocytin, rhodamine and RNase inhibitors
ERCC spike-ins, DNase and proteinase K
Calcium chelators, RNA carriers and RNase inhibitors
Potassium chelators, RNA carriers and DTT
answer: Calcium chelators, RNA carriers and RNase inhibitors
label: Review · internal solution additives

stem: What electrophysiological caveat comes with adding calcium chelators to the Patch-seq internal solution?
choices: They may raise the resting membrane potential
They may broaden action potential width
They may block voltage-gated sodium channels
They may reduce calcium-dependent currents
answer: They may reduce calcium-dependent currents
label: Review · chelator caveat

stem: Because of the RNA-preserving modifications in Patch-seq, how may the electrophysiological recording itself need to change?
choices: It may need to be shorter
It may need a higher temperature
It may need perforated rather than whole-cell access
It may need to be repeated on a second cell
answer: It may need to be shorter
label: Review · recording time

stem: Which collection change has greatly improved RNA yield and transcriptomic quality in recent Patch-seq protocols?
choices: Aspirating the cytosol only, leaving the nucleus
Extracting the nucleus along with the cytosol
Collecting the cell after fixation
Freezing the slice before aspiration
answer: Extracting the nucleus along with the cytosol
label: Review · nucleated patch

stem: Why must a stable pipette-membrane seal be kept while aspirating the cell contents in Patch-seq?
choices: To keep recording during aspiration
To keep biocytin from leaking out of the cell
To avoid contamination from the extracellular solution
To keep the pipette tip from clogging with membrane
answer: To avoid contamination from the extracellular solution
label: Review · seal during aspiration

stem: Besides improved internal and external solutions, what step enhances biocytin staining and morphological reconstruction in Patch-seq?
choices: Fast retraction to reseal the membrane
Fixing the slice before aspiration
Recording at room rather than body temperature
Slow, careful retraction of the pipette
answer: Slow, careful retraction of the pipette
label: Review · morphology recovery

stem: In Patch-seq, what does adding rhodamine to the intracellular solution allow?
choices: Live fluorescent imaging of the neuron before collection
Post hoc reconstruction after fixation and staining
Quantification of RNA yield before sequencing
Detection of glial contamination in the sample
answer: Live fluorescent imaging of the neuron before collection
label: Review · rhodamine

stem: Which non-neuronal cells has Patch-seq been applied to, according to the 2021 review?
choices: Cardiac myocytes
Pancreatic islet cells
Retinal Müller glia
Skeletal muscle fibres
answer: Pancreatic islet cells
label: Review · non-neuronal

stem: In human and nonhuman primate tissue, how is Patch-seq extraction pressure adjusted?
choices: Per cell, typically lower for larger cells
Fixed for each species, higher than in mouse
Per cell, typically higher for larger cells
Fixed for each slice, set by tissue age
answer: Per cell, typically higher for larger cells
label: Review · extraction pressure

stem: What is the aspiration concern for a neuron with many projections embedded in the tissue?
choices: Applying maximal pressure to reach distal dendrites
Collecting the processes separately from the soma
Avoiding aspiration and collecting the nucleus only
Balancing pressure so delicate processes are not torn
answer: Balancing pressure so delicate processes are not torn
label: Review · many projections

stem: Besides high-resolution live imaging, what main advantage does culture-based Patch-seq of iPSC-derived neurons have?
choices: RNA can be collected from the whole neuron, neurites included
Thousands of neurons can be profiled in a single day
Recordings can last for hours without any RNA loss
Glial contamination of the sample is reliably absent
answer: RNA can be collected from the whole neuron, neurites included
label: Review · iPSC cultures

stem: Which scRNAseq library approaches can Patch-seq be combined with?
choices: Droplet-based methods, not plate-based ones
Tube- or plate-based methods, not droplet-based ones
Both droplet- and plate-based methods equally
Only single-nucleus droplet methods
answer: Tube- or plate-based methods, not droplet-based ones
label: Review · library compatibility

stem: Where can synthetic ERCC spike-ins be introduced in a Patch-seq workflow?
choices: Only after library amplification, before sequencing
Only in the extracellular bath during recording
At cDNA synthesis or in the recording internal solution
Only at the final sequencing step on the flow cell
answer: At cDNA synthesis or in the recording internal solution
label: Review · spike-ins

stem: What advantage do full-length cDNA protocols (Smart-seq2, SMART-seq v4) have over UMI-based protocols for Patch-seq?
choices: Absolute molecule counts free of amplification bias
Lower cost per cell than any UMI-based method
Compatibility with droplet-based capture methods
Higher sensitivity and splice-variant coverage
answer: Higher sensitivity and splice-variant coverage
label: Review · full-length cDNA

stem: What advantage do UMI-based protocols have over full-length cDNA protocols for Patch-seq?
choices: Absolute molecule counts, correcting amplification bias
Higher sensitivity per cell at equal sequencing depth
Full-length coverage for splice-variant analysis
Compatibility with nucleated patch collection
answer: Absolute molecule counts, correcting amplification bias
label: Review · UMI

stem: What does the Smart-Seq3 protocol offer Patch-seq?
choices: Droplet-based throughput with full-length coverage
Full-length coverage combined with UMIs
UMIs without any reverse transcription
Joint genome and transcriptome profiling
answer: Full-length coverage combined with UMIs
label: Review · Smart-Seq3

stem: What accounts for most of the cost of running Patch-seq experiments?
choices: Electrophysiology rigs and amplifiers
Morphological reconstruction labour
cDNA/library preparation and sequencing
Animal husbandry and slice preparation
answer: cDNA/library preparation and sequencing
label: Review · cost driver

stem: Roughly what does the commercial SMART-seq v4 kit cost per cell for Patch-seq, excluding sequencing?
choices: About $20
label: Review · kit cost

stem: How do low-level bioinformatics pipelines for Patch-seq relate to those for dissociated scRNAseq?
choices: They are typically identical
They need a dedicated aligner for aspirated RNA
They skip gene-level quantification
They quantify only mitochondrial reads
answer: They are typically identical
label: Review · processing

stem: Up to roughly what share of Patch-seq reads come from unspliced (presumably nuclear) transcripts?
choices: About 5%
About 50%
About 20%
About 90%
answer: About 50%
label: Review · unspliced reads

stem: Given its high share of unspliced reads, how is gene expression best quantified in Patch-seq?
choices: Using exonic read counts only
Using intronic read counts only
Using both exonic and intronic read counts
Using UMI counts of spliced reads only
answer: Using both exonic and intronic read counts
label: Review · exonic+intronic

stem: What kind of off-target contamination has often been observed in Patch-seq samples from acute brain slices?
choices: Bacterial, from the recording rig
Mitochondrial, from damaged neurons
Blood cells, from slice vasculature
Glial, such as microglial markers
answer: Glial, such as microglial markers
label: Review · contamination

stem: Why is mapping Patch-seq transcriptomes onto a dissociation-based scRNAseq reference a key classification step?
choices: The reference has orders of magnitude more cells
The reference has no contamination from neuropil
The reference includes morphology for every cell
The reference was sequenced with the same kit
answer: The reference has orders of magnitude more cells
label: Review · reference mapping

stem: Which kind of method typically allows accurate mapping of Patch-seq cells to a reference atlas despite expression differences?
choices: Electrophysiology-based clustering
Correlation-based methods
Morphology-based matching
Spike-in normalised thresholds
answer: Correlation-based methods
label: Review · mapping method

stem: Why is morphology hard to include in multimodal Patch-seq frameworks such as reduced-rank regression and coupled autoencoders?
choices: Morphology does not correlate with gene expression
Morphology files are too large to process
Fewer cells and difficult feature-vector representation
Morphology is recorded only in culture preparations
answer: Fewer cells and difficult feature-vector representation
label: Review · morphology in models

stem: What crucial advantage does Patch-seq sample collection have over dissociation-based scRNAseq, despite lower throughput?
choices: Its transcriptomes contain no nuclear RNA at all
Its libraries cost less per cell to prepare
Its RNA yield per cell is considerably higher
The exact source cell of each transcriptome is known
answer: The exact source cell of each transcriptome is known
label: Review · targeted sampling

stem: What did Patch-seq reveal about cortical excitatory neurons derived from a common early progenitor?
choices: They are no more likely to share a type than random neighbours
They almost always share the same transcriptomic type
They share a type, but only within the same layer
They share morphology but not their transcriptomic type
answer: They are no more likely to share a type than random neighbours
label: Review · clonal lineage

stem: What did Patch-seq of excitatory neurons from later progenitor pools reveal about apical intermediate progenitors?
choices: They contribute a transcriptionally distinct layer 5 subtype
They contribute a transcriptionally distinct layer 2/3 subtype
They give rise only to interneurons
Their progeny are indistinguishable from other layer 2/3 neurons
answer: They contribute a transcriptionally distinct layer 2/3 subtype
label: Review · intermediate progenitors

stem: Combined with transplantation experiments, Patch-seq identified which signalling pathway in the temporal specification of apical neuronal progenitors?
choices: Notch
Sonic hedgehog
Wnt
BMP
answer: Wnt
label: Review · Wnt

stem: Where were the morphoelectrically and transcriptomically distinct neurons identified by the first multimodal Patch-seq studies?
choices: Cortical layers 5 and 6
Hippocampal area CA1
Dorsal striatum
Cortical layers 1 and 2
answer: Cortical layers 1 and 2
label: Review · first multimodal studies

stem: At what scale had the largest multimodal Patch-seq classification efforts in mouse visual and motor cortex profiled neurons by 2021?
choices: Thousands of neurons
Dozens of neurons
Hundreds of neurons
Hundreds of thousands of neurons
answer: Thousands of neurons
label: Review · scale

stem: What did Patch-seq of striatal interneurons uncover about the link between transcriptome and electrophysiology?
choices: Discrete types with sharply separated firing
Continuous gradients matching graded electrophysiology
No relation between expression and firing
Gradients in expression but uniform firing
answer: Continuous gradients matching graded electrophysiology
label: Review · striatum

stem: What unexpected developmental change did Patch-seq find in hippocampal parvalbumin-positive interneurons?
choices: Loss of parvalbumin expression
Onset of serotonin receptor expression
Onset of hemoglobin expression
A switch to excitatory neurotransmitter genes
answer: Onset of hemoglobin expression
label: Review · PV interneurons

stem: What did multimodal analysis of layer 4 interneurons in mouse visual and somatosensory cortex suggest?
choices: Transcriptomic type fully predicts morphology
Electrophysiology is identical across areas
Visual and somatosensory types share no genes
Transcriptomically similar neurons differ by cortical area
answer: Transcriptomically similar neurons differ by cortical area
label: Review · layer 4 interneurons

stem: What overall picture of cell-type identification emerges from cross-modality Patch-seq studies?
choices: No single feature suffices to identify a cell type
Transcriptome alone suffices to identify a cell type
Electrophysiology alone suffices to identify a cell type
Morphology alone suffices to identify a cell type
answer: No single feature suffices to identify a cell type
label: Review · no single feature

stem: In the motor-cortex Patch-seq study, how well were transcriptomic types separated in morphoelectric space?
choices: Close types separated; broad families overlapped
Broad families separated; close types did not
All types, broad and close, separated cleanly
Neither broad families nor close types separated
answer: Broad families separated; close types did not
label: Review · motor cortex

stem: What did Patch-seq show about corticocortical projection neurons of the visual cortex that form a single transcriptomic cluster?
choices: They share identical projection targets
They split into distinct types by firing pattern alone
They split into distinct types by projections and connectivity
They are a mix of excitatory and inhibitory cells
answer: They split into distinct types by projections and connectivity
label: Review · projection neurons

stem: What distinguished rat CA3 CCK+ interneurons with different excitability properties, per Patch-seq?
choices: Distinct isoforms of voltage-gated sodium channel pore subunits
Different levels of 5-HT3 receptor subunits
Different amounts of parvalbumin expression
Distinct isoforms of Kv channel auxiliary subunits
answer: Distinct isoforms of Kv channel auxiliary subunits
label: Review · CCK interneurons

stem: How was Patch-seq used to study functional heterogeneity in human iPSC-derived neuronal cultures?
choices: A classifier trained on it predicted function in scRNAseq data
It recorded every neuron across thousands of cultures
It mapped the cultures onto an adult cortex atlas
It sorted neurons by morphology before any recording
answer: A classifier trained on it predicted function in scRNAseq data
label: Review · iPSC classifier

stem: How did CCK+ interneurons lacking 5-HT3 receptor mRNA still respond to serotonin?
choices: Through metabotropic 5-HT1A receptors on the soma
Through gap-junction coupling to neighbouring cells
Through serotonin transporter currents
Through presynaptic glutamate release onto them
answer: Through gap-junction coupling to neighbouring cells
label: Review · serotonin

stem: Which electrophysiological property correlates strongly with Kcna1 (Kv1.1) mRNA among hippocampal and striatal inhibitory cell types?
choices: Resting membrane potential
Input resistance
Action potential width
Spike-frequency adaptation
answer: Action potential width
label: Review · Kcna1

stem: What did the pancreatic islet Patch-seq study additionally show about tissue preparation?
choices: Patch-seq needs freshly dispersed cells
Patch-seq works on fixed tissue
Patch-seq works only on cultured islets
Patch-seq works on cryopreserved tissue
answer: Patch-seq works on cryopreserved tissue
label: Review · cryopreserved

stem: Besides low throughput and being laborious to master, what third challenge of Patch-seq does the review name?
choices: It requires interdisciplinary skills
It cannot be used on human tissue
It needs droplet-based sequencing
It cannot recover morphology
answer: It requires interdisciplinary skills
label: Review · challenges

stem: What makes Patch-seq unique compared with combining separate higher-throughput single-modality datasets post hoc?
choices: It profiles more cells per experiment
All modalities come from the same cell
It needs no reference atlas
It needs no computational integration
answer: All modalities come from the same cell
label: Review · uniqueness

stem: What did Patch-seq on neurosurgically resected human tissue identify?
choices: Increased GABAergic neuron diversity in human cortex
Reduced glutamatergic diversity relative to mouse
Increased glutamatergic neuron diversity in human cortex
Identical cell types to mouse cortex
answer: Increased glutamatergic neuron diversity in human cortex
label: Review · human cortex

stem: Which protocol does the review cite for separating mRNA after collection so that genomic modalities could be added to Patch-seq?
choices: Smart-Seq3
CEL-Seq2
STRT-C1
G&T
answer: G&T
label: Review · future modalities

stem: Which area does the review call yet untapped for Patch-seq?
choices: Transcriptomic mechanisms of synapse function and plasticity
Transcriptomic correlates of sensory responses in vivo
Cell-type classification in the motor cortex
Molecular correlates of developmental lineage
answer: Transcriptomic mechanisms of synapse function and plasticity
label: Review · untapped area

stem: What would multi-Patch-seq experiments add, according to the review?
choices: Higher throughput through pooled sequencing of cells
Direct correlation of gene expression with connectivity
Joint genome and transcriptome profiling per cell
Recording in freely moving animals
answer: Direct correlation of gene expression with connectivity
label: Review · multi-Patch-seq
